title: Mount St Helens observers killed by heat miles away
summary: Matt LaCroix tells of Mount St Helens observers killed by heat miles away, about 1980 at Washington, D.C., and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: watch documentaries on Mount St Helens right when it erupted people were 5 10 miles away observing it

plain: Matt LaCroix, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast who talks about ancient catastrophes, points to the 1980 eruption of Mount St Helens, a volcano in Washington State. According to LaCroix, documentaries show that people watching from five to ten miles away were killed by the heat. He tells it to show how far the force of a natural disaster can reach, which would matter for his ideas about a great catastrophe long ago.
